question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed experimental Claw package and lifecycle contract as the direction for portable complete-agent bundles across OpenClaw and ClawHub?
rationale: The patch is an RFC defining new user-facing concepts, CLI behavior, package formats, and cross-repository ownership boundaries; correctness review cannot determine whether that product surface belongs in the roadmap.

options.title: Sponsor the experimental contract
options.body: Accept the Claws direction, name an owner for the implementation stack, and retain the explicit experimental gate and compatibility review before each landing PR.

options.title: Narrow the RFC
options.body: Limit the proposal to a smaller manifest or local workflow before accepting package publication, registry, and cross-owner lifecycle commitments.

options.title: Decline core adoption for now
options.body: Keep the component concepts on existing plugin, skill, and ClawHub surfaces until a maintainer-sponsored need justifies a new core lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the experimental contract
recommendation.body: Accept the Claws direction, name an owner for the implementation stack, and retain the explicit experimental gate and compatibility review before each landing PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The available review record shows direct engagement with the central MCP and package-boundary questions.
